title: Tenant-aware probabilistic degradation and traffic shepherd for safe service degradation
creator: Priya Nair
description: Design and implement a tenant-aware degradation system that probabilistically routes a small fraction of traffic to degraded modes under early warning signals, and fully trips only when multi-signal thresholds are met. The goal is to avoid hard failovers and provide safe fallbacks (cached responses, quantized model tier, or informative errors) while preserving SLOs for unaffected tenants and enabling quick recovery.
background: Recent incidents showed that single-metric trips (p99 latency spikes) cause mass fallbacks that cascade across services and increase unit cost when we immediately switch entire tenants to fallback models. We need a system that: 1) makes early, low-impact decisions (soft trips) that validate degradation behavior; 2) isolates tenants and models to reduce blast radius; 3) uses probabilistic sampling to check degraded-mode quality before scaling the fallback up.
proposed_solution:
We will implement a multi-layered circuit mechanism with the following components:

1) Circuit Score (per resource): compute a rolling score that aggregates multiple signals with weights: error_rate (0.5), p99_latency (0.3), infra_backpressure (0.1), kernel_retries (0.1). Score in [0,1].

2) Soft Trip (probabilistic degradation): when score > soft_threshold (e.g., 0.45) for window W_soft (30s), enable probabilistic degradation for that tenant-resource: sample p = min(0.05 + (score - soft_threshold) * 0.6, 0.5) of traffic is served in degraded mode. Degraded mode options: cached_prefix_response, quantized-model-serve, token-limited streaming, or structured guidance response.

3) Hard Trip: if score > hard_threshold (e.g., 0.8) for W_hard (2m) OR soft_trip failure rate (degraded-mode error) > fail_threshold, flip circuit to OPEN for the tenant-resource and route all traffic to a pre-configured fallback. Hard trips follow exponential cool-down with jitter (cooldown_base=60s, multiplier=2, jitter=0.2).

4) Safe Fallbacks: define per-tenant fallback policies with strict SLAs: a) tenant-level priority: fallback to cached+model_sample for high-priority tenants, b) for low-priority tenants allow rate-limited 503 with retry guidance, c) always preserve PII by using KMS-verified fallbacks for Private deployments.

5) Traffic Shepherd: centralized controller that manages global allocation across regions and model-capacity pools. On regional pressure, shepherd will 1) redistribute sampled soft-trip traffic to underutilized regions; 2) temporarily increase sampling to validate cross-region degraded mode; 3) if redistribute fails, apply tenant isolation policies and circuit open.

6) Hysteresis & Recovery: require a stable improvement period (window W_recover, e.g., 3m) before scaling down degradation; recovery should be gradual (50% -> 25% -> 0% sampling) with canary checks that route small percentages back to primary mode to verify improvements.

7) Telemetry: emit circuit_score, soft_trip_rate, degraded_mode_error, hard_trip_count, cooldown_remaining, fallback_type as standardized metrics and traces for debugging and postmortems.

This approach balances early mitigation with safety checks and keeps blast radius small by isolating by tenant+resource+model.
config_examples:
Example policy YAML (stored in config service or tenant policy):

policy_id: probabilistic-degrade-v1
scope: tenant+model
soft_threshold: 0.45
hard_threshold: 0.80
window_soft_seconds: 30
window_hard_seconds: 120
soft_max_sample: 0.5
cooldown_base_seconds: 60
cooldown_multiplier: 2
cooldown_jitter: 0.2
fallback_chain:
  - name: cached_prefix_response
    max_age_seconds: 900
  - name: quantized_small
    quantize_profile: q4_0
    max_qps: 200
  - name: informative_503
    retry_after: 60

Note: controller will compile tenant policy into runtime rules per-resource (e.g., model, datastore dependency).
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests for circuit scoring logic with synthetic signal streams pass (error scenarios, latency spikes, kernel retries).
Canary rollout of probabilistic degradation for one non-critical tenant shows proper sampling and metrics (degraded_mode_error < 2%).
Hard trip triggers only after sustained multi-signal violation and respects cooldown with jitter in simulated load tests.
Traffic shepherd correctly re-routes sampled traffic to a secondary region in the lab environment under induced regional pressure.
All emitted metrics are available in metrics namespace 'circuit' with dashboards and alerts configured.
Documentation: runbook and per-tenant fallback configuration guide published in Confluence.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy controller and runtime hooks in staging behind a feature flag; enable for internal tenants only.
Phase 2: Canary for one non-critical production tenant (1 day) with high observability; verify degraded_mode_error and recovery behavior.
Phase 3: Expand to 10% of tenants with automated rollback if key alerts fire (degraded_mode_error > 5% or customer_error_rate increases).
Phase 4: Full rollout and monitoring tuning; deprecate legacy single-metric circuit behavior.
Rollback: disable feature flag and gradually revert policies; pre-built rollback playbook in runbook.
monitoring_and_alerting: Primary alerts: hard_trip_rate_per_min > X for > 5m across any region (pager).
Secondary alerts: degraded_mode_error_rate > 5% for high-priority tenants (page).
Warning alerts: circuit_score_delta_in_1m > 0.4 for any tenant-resource (Slack).
Dashboards: tenant heatmap (open circuits, soft_trip_rate), model pool pressure, traffic shepherd re-route counts.
SLOs: measure customer-visible error-rate and p99 latency for primary vs degraded path; ensure fallbacks meet documented degraded SLAs.
test_plan: Signal fuzzing harness to drive combined signals into circuit_score to validate thresholds and hysteresis behavior.
Chaos experiments: simulate regional capacity loss, kernel failures, and KV cache eviction to observe traffic shepherd behavior.
End-to-end tests: synthetic requests that verify per-tenant fallback chains and PII-safe handling for Private deployments.
Load tests: ensure that quantized-model fallbacks behave within their configured max_qps and autoscaling triggers.
open_questions: What should default soft/hard thresholds be for new tenants vs legacy tenants with high throughput?
How do we prioritize fallback types when multiple are available and model-quality budgets differ?
Should traffic shepherd prefer region affinity for latency-sensitive tenants even if another region has spare capacity?
Do we need billing/attribution changes when a tenant is served by degraded-mode (cost delta tracking)?
notes: Opted for a score-based approach to avoid brittle single-metric trips; weights will be tunable via runtime config.
Probabilistic degradation reduces the risk of a bad fallback working at scale; it also gives us sampled telemetry to validate fallback quality.
We must be conservative with sampling for enterprise tenants (explicit opt-in to aggressive fallback).
This ticket ties closely to the autoscaler and model-pools work (ENG-32844).
